title: Brain MR angiography: the Circle of Willis and intracranial aneurysms
description: 3D time-of-flight MR angiograms of the head at native resolution. Thirteen patients with unruptured intracranial aneurysms, each outlined voxel by voxel by a radiologist and double-checked by a senior neuroradiologist (Lausanne TOF-MRA Aneurysm Cohort), and six people without aneurysms whose Circle of Willis was labelled artery by artery by the TopCoW challenge annotators, chosen to show a complete circle and the common variants (fetal-type posterior cerebral artery, missing A1 or anterior communicating artery). Converted from NIfTI with the geometry of the NIfTI affine.

provenanceDetail.method: Voxel-wise outline drawn slice by slice in the axial plane (ITK-SNAP) by a radiologist with 2 years of neuroimaging experience and double-checked by a senior neuroradiologist with over 15 years of experience (Di Noto et al. 2023). The mask is on the TOF grid; traced per slice with skimage find_contours (0.5) into image_px [col, row].
provenanceDetail.note: 8 slices; mask volume 132 mm3; largest extent 7.7 mm; 1 connected part(s).

referenceTargets.unassessedNote: Only the aneurysm sac is outlined. The parent artery, the neck and any other finding are not referenced; the dataset does not record which artery the aneurysm arises from.
referenceTargets.teachingNote: Unruptured aneurysm, about 8 mm across in the outline. On time-of-flight MRA the flowing blood in the sac is bright like the parent artery; slow or turbulent flow and thrombus can make parts of it less bright.
